response:
The Carnot engine efficiency is \(1 - \frac{T_C}{T_H} = 1 - \frac{300}{900} = \frac{2}{3}\). Work done = efficiency × heat absorbed = \(\frac{2}{3} \times 100 = \frac{200}{3} \approx 66.6666666667\) cal.

The mixture of 0.1 mol He (γ=5/3) and 0.2 mol N₂ (γ=7/5) has an effective γ = \(\frac{0.1\cdot\frac{5}{2}R + 0.2\cdot\frac{7}{2}R}{0.1\cdot\frac{3}{2}R + 0.2\cdot\frac{5}{2}R} = \frac{19}{13}\). Initial pressure \(P_1 = \frac{nRT_1}{V_1} = \frac{0.3 \times 0.08205746 \times 300}{4} = 1.84629285\) atm. After a 1% reduction in volume, \(V_2 = 0.99V_1\), so \(P_2 = P_1 \left(\frac{V_1}{V_2}\right)^{\gamma} = 1.84629285 \times \left(\frac{100}{99}\right)^{19/13} \approx 1.8736131215\) atm.

ANSWER: 66.6666666667,1.8736131215
